text:
ROUTE 1 IS NARROWER THAN I SAID TWENTY MINUTES AGO. I checked the synthetic model before recommending someone spend time on it, and it is a toy.

  CodecGens.scala:239   val source: StorySource = StorySource.fromText(text, Some("Tiny"))

IT IS LITERALLY NAMED "Tiny". Its companion recall graph runs over a two-sentence transcript -- "A woman went home. Then she slept." -- and `validated` is that draft put through StoryValidator with the default policy.

SO RENDERING IT WOULD PROVE EXACTLY ONE THING, AND I SHOULD HAVE SAID SO: that Edition.build accepts a second VALUE without crashing, and carries no hard-coded War of the Ghosts identifiers. That is a real smoke test and it is worth an hour -- if the renderer has quietly grown WOG-shaped assumptions, a Tiny model finds them immediately and cheaply.

IT WOULD NOT PROVE what I implied, which is that the renderer produces something a reader would want to look at for a story it was not built around. A two-sentence model renders a nearly empty page. Passing that tells you the code paths execute; it tells you nothing about whether the atlas, the codex pagination, or the annotation overlay do anything USEFUL on unfamiliar material.

RELABEL IT ACCORDINGLY, and this matters because the whole point of the exercise was to stop "already general" being an untested claim -- replacing it with a differently untested claim would be worse than leaving it alone:

  ROUTE 1 = SMOKE TEST for hard-coded assumptions. Cheap, real, do it.
  THE GENERALITY QUESTION stays open until a model of comparable richness to WOG is rendered, and
  that means route 2 -- public-domain text plus generated attempts -- not route 1.

I have now corrected my own advice on this bead three times in an hour: hand-authoring is not required (owner), the attempts are what a generator produces (measured), and route 1 is a smoke test rather than a generality proof (measured). Each correction came from reading a file rather than reasoning about it, which is the only method that has worked today.
